sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Checks Python and creates environment
sections.what: Checks that Python 3.9 or newer is installed, creates a private package folder called venv, activates it, and upgrades pip. It stops with a message if any step fails.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps project packages separate and makes sure the Python version is new enough for the code.
sections.watch_out: The version check depends on grep -P, which the default macOS grep may not support, so an old Python could slip through.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Installs packages and prints next steps
sections.what: Installs everything listed in requirements.txt, creates the exports folder, checks for the optional Ollama tool and lists its models if present, and prints the steps for opening the notebooks. If the install fails, it reruns with full output and then stops.
sections.why: Likely reason: Ollama is optional because the app can also use OpenAI, so the check only reports and does not block setup.
sections.watch_out: The printed instructions name notebook and guide files that this packet does not show, so they must exist or the steps will mislead a new user.

summary: Setup script for macOS and Linux that checks Python, creates a private package area, installs the project's packages, and prints next steps.
purpose: Lets a user set up the project with one command instead of several manual steps.
why: Likely reason: a single script avoids mistakes from creating the environment and installing packages by hand.
how: Checks that Python is version 3.9 or newer, creates a venv folder, activates it, upgrades pip, installs everything in requirements.txt (retrying with full output if that fails), creates the exports folder, checks for Ollama and lists its models if found, and prints instructions.
inputs: The Python 3 program on the machine, requirements.txt in the same folder, and optionally Ollama.
outputs: A venv folder with packages installed, an exports folder, and messages in the terminal.
risks: The version check uses grep with the -P option, which the default macOS grep may not support, so an old Python could pass without warning. A failed package install stops the script. The activation only lasts while the script runs.
debug: Run the script again and read the last message before it stops. Check the Python version with python3 --version. For package errors, read the verbose output shown on the retry. Confirm the venv folder exists.
